title: In Valeria Luiselli's New Novel, the Past Never Stays Behind
gist: A review of Valeria Luiselli's July 2026 novel Beginning, Middle, End, which follows a divorced novelist and her 12-year-old daughter across Sicily to return a Roman mosaic taken to Mexico in the 1920s. The reviewer reads it as showing that the past never stays behind and that stories belong to whoever picks them up next.

insights.claim: The novel follows a mother and her 12-year-old daughter driving across Sicily to return a mosaic that the girl's great-grandmother Nanna dug out of a Roman villa and carried to Mexico in the 1920s, spanning four generations.
insights.speaker: DANIELA ORDOÑEZ DELGADO
insights.so_what: Basic facts for catalogue and recommendation purposes.

insights.claim: The book is a Knopf release of July 2026, 464 pages.
insights.speaker: DANIELA ORDOÑEZ DELGADO

insights.claim: Luiselli's long-running subject is geographic borders, from the US-Mexico border in Lost Children Archive (2019) to Sicily as a crossing point between Africa and Europe where migrants await asylum officers.
insights.speaker: DANIELA ORDOÑEZ DELGADO
insights.so_what: Frames migration themes across her work.
insights.locator: Geographic borders are one of Luiselli's long subjects

insights.claim: The novel treats memory and imagination as blending so that people cannot later tell them apart; the daughter's 'memory' of nearly drowning in a guitar-shaped pool is actually a scene from her mother's novel.
insights.speaker: DANIELA ORDOÑEZ DELGADO
insights.so_what: Core literary device of the book.
insights.quote: in such a way that we will not know how to tell things apart one day

insights.claim: Forgetting runs in the family, and the mother uses translation of memorized book passages as a temporary dike against the grandmother's cognitive decline.
insights.speaker: DANIELA ORDOÑEZ DELGADO
insights.so_what: Links translation and dementia in the narrative.
insights.quote: a dike, even if temporary, against forgetting
insights.locator: Forgetting runs in the family, too

insights.claim: The reviewer concludes the book shows the past never stays behind and that a story belongs to whoever picks it up next; inheritance running both ways means the book can only be a middle.
insights.speaker: DANIELA ORDOÑEZ DELGADO
insights.quote: What Beginning, Middle, End never denies is that a story belongs to whoever picks it up next.
